facts.raw_span: an 18-hour history of generalized abdominal pain
fever (39 °C)
vomiting
constipation
a rigid abdomen and diffuse severe tenderness
soft stool without blood
C-reactive protein was elevated at 134.5 mg/L
air–fluid levels in the small bowel and dilated large-bowel loops
a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops
a hyperdense midline mass above the bladder
normal hemoglobin, white-cell and platelet counts
normal prothrombin time, INR, glucose, creatinine, urea, sodium, and potassium

support_spans: air–fluid levels in the small bowel and dilated large-bowel loops
a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops
a hyperdense midline mass above the bladder
concepts.why: The presence of air-fluid levels, a hyperechoic mass surrounded by intestinal loops, and a hyperdense midline mass above the bladder are characteristic of intussusception.

support_spans: a rigid abdomen and diffuse severe tenderness
C-reactive protein was elevated at 134.5 mg/L
contradict_spans: a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops
concepts.why: The presence of a rigid abdomen, diffuse severe tenderness, and elevated C-reactive protein are suggestive of appendicitis, but the mass in the hypogastric region is more characteristic of intussusception.

support_spans: air–fluid levels in the small bowel and dilated large-bowel loops
contradict_spans: a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops
concepts.why: The presence of air-fluid levels in the small bowel is suggestive of a small bowel obstruction, which can be caused by Meckel's diverticulum, but the mass in the hypogastric region is more characteristic of intussusception.

support_spans: a rigid abdomen and diffuse severe tenderness
contradict_spans: a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops
concepts.why: The presence of a rigid abdomen and diffuse severe tenderness is suggestive of ovarian torsion, but the mass in the hypogastric region is more characteristic of intussusception.

support_spans: C-reactive protein was elevated at 134.5 mg/L
contradict_spans: a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops
concepts.why: The presence of elevated C-reactive protein is suggestive of inflammatory bowel disease, but the mass in the hypogastric region is more characteristic of intussusception.

rationales.F05: Abdominal tenderness is common in several conditions, but its presence helps to rule in intussusception and appendicitis.
rationales.F06: The absence of blood in the stool makes appendicitis less likely, but its presence is not specific enough to rule in intussusception.
rationales.F07: Elevated C-reactive protein is a non-specific marker of inflammation, but its presence helps to rule in conditions like intussusception and inflammatory bowel disease.
rationales.F08: Air-fluid levels in the small bowel and dilated large-bowel loops are highly suggestive of intussusception.
rationales.F09: A hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops is highly suggestive of intussusception.
rationales.F10: A hyperdense midline mass above the bladder is highly suggestive of intussusception.
